definitions.danger: For LuckyJ's actual discard, max(state[danger_s/t/k][LuckyJ seat][tile_index] / 10000).

table_threats.quiet: no riichi and no opponent with any melds
table_threats.1_meld_opponent_max: no riichi; max opponent meld count is 1
table_threats.2_meld_opponent: no riichi; max opponent meld count is 2
table_threats.3plus_meld_opponent: no riichi; max opponent meld count is 3+
table_threats.single_riichi: exactly one opponent riichi and no opponent with 2+ melds
table_threats.riichi_plus_more: 2+ opponent riichi, or at least one riichi plus an opponent with 2+ melds

definitions.max_threat_opponent: Riichi seats are chosen first when any opponent has riichi; otherwise the opponent(s) with max meld count are chosen, tied by higher NAGA tenpai estimate. Quiet tables use the highest tenpai estimate among opponents.
definitions.meld_count_tracking: chi/pon/daiminkan and ankan increment meld count; kakan upgrades without increment, matching scripts/build_point_examples.py collect_examples().
definitions.turn: opponent turn = len(discards[opponent]) + 1 at LuckyJ's decision.

own_state.closed_tenpai: no own melds, not already riichi, raw shanten <= 0 on the 13-tile hand plus draw
own_state.closed_1_shanten: no own melds, not already riichi, raw shanten == 1
own_state.closed_2plus_shanten: no own melds, not already riichi, raw shanten >= 2
own_state.own_open_hand: LuckyJ has at least one meld; shanten intentionally not computed
own_state.own_riichi: LuckyJ is already in riichi; included because every tsumo state with real_dahai+dahai_pred is counted, but it is not a free push/fold choice

definitions.immediate_riichi_reaction: For each opponent riichi declaration, LuckyJ's next tsumo discard is tested as genbutsu if its tile index appears in that riichi player's river by then; multiple pending riichi declarations create multiple observations.
definitions.n_fields: In danger metrics, total_states counts matching decisions; n counts decisions with usable danger; rates use n. In genbutsu metrics, n counts reaction observations.

open_hand_trigger.scope: no-riichi states where the max opponent has exactly 2 melds or 3+ melds

vs_riichi.scope: states classified as single_riichi or riichi_plus_more

proposed_rules: Against a 2-meld open hand, start pricing defense by the second row: turn 7-12 push rate was 44.1% (n=8529), and turn 13+ was 39.2% (n=4522).
Against 3+ melds, treat the hand as a live threat immediately; LuckyJ's >5% danger push rate was 56.8% (n=111) in the earliest populated bucket.
With an engine tenpai read on 2+ melds, the first decile where push fell below 50% was 90-100% (42.8%, n=17730).
Versus riichi, tenpai is the main license to continue: closed tenpai pushed 61.3% (n=1360), while closed 2-shanten pushed 20.3% (n=6036).
Versus riichi, downgrade sharply outside tenpai: closed 1-shanten pushed 33.6% (n=6019), and closed 3+ shanten pushed 14.2% (n=3421).
In the last 20 tiles versus riichi, don't chase from far away: 1-shanten pushed 22.9% (n=1768), 2-shanten pushed 13.4% (n=1693).
First discard after an opponent riichi should usually be genbutsu unless the hand is real: tenpai genbutsu 32.6% (n=371), 1-shanten 55.5% (n=1792), 2-shanten 64.3% (n=1433).
